target.title: feat(cli): list and resolve pending approvals headlessly
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
There was no headless way to answer a pending exec/plugin/system-agent approval: `openclaw approvals` managed policy only, and `/approve <id>` requires a chat surface. Operators on SSH or in scripts had to open a UI.

## Why This Change Was Made
`openclaw approvals pending` lists pending approvals across all three kinds (table + `--json`), and `openclaw approvals resolve <id> <allow-once|allow-always|deny>` resolves through the unified `approval.resolve` RPC with first-answer-wins semantics: idempotent success when already resolved with the same decision, clear non-zero errors for conflicts/not-found/expired. Approval ids are treated as opaque and preserved verbatim (never trimmed); terminal-unsafe ids (hostile ANSI/control content is possible because explicit ids are stored verbatim) render as lossless copyable `id64_` tokens while normal ids display raw; ill-formed-Unicode ids the unified schema cannot address are skipped; system-agent entries show only their reviewer-safe presentation (title/description), never the host-local operation; resolution authenticates with `operator.admin`/`operator.approvals` scopes without forcing a device identity onto loopback shared-auth sessions. Docs gain the new subcommands plus a "minimal scopes for third-party clients" note.

## User Impact
Approvals become fully operable from a terminal or script. No gateway or protocol changes.

## Evidence
- Focused CLI suite green (30+ tests incl. hostile-id rendering, verbatim-id preservation, ambiguity guard, race/idempotency outcomes, JSON shape, system-agent redaction).
- Remote typechecks + docs-list green; git diff --check clean.
- Structured autoreview: clean after six hardening rounds (opaque-id preservation, token losslessness, scope/auth, redaction boundary).
